Damayantī
------------------------------------------
Damayantī is one of the five ideal ladies extolled for her wifely virtues along with सीता and सावित्री. As per the story given in the Vanaparva (chapter 52 onwards, called Nalopākhyāna) of the Mahābhārata, she was the daughter of the king Bhīmabhūpala (of Vidarbha) and the wife of the king नल (of Niṣadha).
For more details see NALA.

dama
(‘control’)
------------------------------------------
All the Hindu philosophical systems which accept the authority of the वेदस्, posit मोक्ष or लिबेरतिओन् from transmigratory existence, as the final goal of life. This becomes possible only when one realises one’s real nature as the आत्मन्, the Self, of the nature of pure चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्, totally different from the body-मिन्द् complex. This, again, involves a lot of spiritual struggle wherein one has to conquer the pulls and pushes of the powerful sense-organs and sense-objects. ‘Dama’ is the technical term given to this aspect of spiritual discipline, by the Vedāntic treatises, especially the उपनिषद्स् and the Bhagavadgītā.
It is generally defined as restraining and pulling back the external sense-organs like the eyes and the ears from all those objects which do not aid the meditation on the आत्मन्, but try to distract and disturb the मिन्द्.
See also SĀDHANACATUṢṬAYA.
